title: The Printing Press and Information Revolution
text: The printing press, invented by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, Germany, around 1440, was one of the most transformative inventions in human history. Using movable metal type, it dramatically reduced the cost and time required to produce books and pamphlets. Before the printing press, books were hand-copied by scribes and accessible mainly to the clergy and nobility. Within fifty years of its invention, over 20 million books had been printed in Europe. The printing press played a crucial role in the Protestant Reformation by allowing Martin Luther's ideas to spread rapidly, and it accelerated the Renaissance and Scientific Revolution by disseminating new knowledge.
